verdict.rationale: Adyen Issuing documents its own transaction rules, which automatically approve or decline authorizations that don't meet configured business requirements. That is a native event-triggered rule capability, but it covers only one event type (card authorizations) and two actions (approve/decline). Relayed authorization and webhooks are developer building blocks and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: rules triggered by events other than authorizations, actions beyond approve/decline (e.g., suspending a card or notifying), documentation of rule conditions and configuration depth, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Create transaction rules to automatically approve or decline authorizations.
You can use transaction rules to configure a logic that automatically declines an authorization that does not meet your business' requirements.
